A1.justification: Both 23-page PDFs describe the same SIC research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite some pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and explanation-evaluation results on Pascal VOC, Stanford Dogs, RSNA, and FunnyBirds, including qualitative and latent-space analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a SIC evaluation on CUB-200-2011 and an additional ProtoPNet training-recipe result.

M1.justification: SIC's architecture, support selection, similarity aggregation, and training objective remain unchanged. Naming the existing 'closest cluster' procedure and explicitly identifying the B-cos similarity layer clarify implementation. Removing alternative activation examples does not change the ReLU implementation already specified in v2.

E1.justification: New Appendix A.3.2 evaluates SIC on CUB-200-2011, extending real-image fine-grained classification coverage to birds. Pascal VOC, Stanford Dogs, RSNA, and FunnyBirds remain.

E2.justification: The comparator methods remain black-box networks, NW-Head, ProtoPNet, BagNet, and B-cos. The added Stanford Dogs row changes ProtoPNet's training recipe, without establishing a different comparison method. The new CUB comparison also uses the already-present ProtoPNet.

E3.justification: Table A.2 adds a ProtoPNet/ResNet50 evaluation using the training recipe from Donnelly et al. [9], alongside the original recipe from Chen et al. [8]. The new CUB evaluation specifies official splits and cropped ROIs. Explicitly assigning balanced accuracy to RSNA clarifies previously ambiguous wording.

E4.justification: Table A.2 adds a limited training-recipe sensitivity check for ProtoPNet on Stanford Dogs by reporting outcomes under two recipes. The FunnyBirds explanation tests, qualitative failure cases, and latent-space/debugging analyses remain unchanged; the CUB addition provides benchmark accuracy only.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additions retain point-estimate reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table A.2 adds ProtoPNet's 74.70% Stanford Dogs accuracy under the alternative recipe, retaining the original 49.24% and SIC's 83.46%. Appendix A.3.2 adds SIC's 79.8% CUB accuracy and cites ProtoPNet's 76.1–80.2% range. These are additional results, not replacements or same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The B-cos definitions, derivations, and faithfulness arguments for the six axioms and support vectors in Appendices A.1–A.2 are unchanged. Changes to the displayed Nadaraya-Watson probability formula are typesetting differences.

C1.justification: Section 5 changes a claim that debugging and end-user understanding benefits were demonstrated to a statement that results suggest explanations may provide those benefits. The central claims about faithful local/global explanations and competitive accuracy remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion interprets the existing examples more cautiously as suggesting potential benefits for developers and end-users. Existing explanations of model behavior and limitations concerning support-vector overhead, class scaling, and difficult RSNA representations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a SIC implementation link in Section 3 and explicitly states in Appendix A.3 that the similarity function uses a B-cos linear layer. It also supplies the alternative ProtoPNet recipe reference and CUB split/cropping information. These are limited reproducibility additions.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Welinder et al. bird-dataset reference and uses the already-cited Donnelly et al. work to identify an alternative training recipe. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; subsequent reference renumbering is not a substantive change.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify parameter-count approximations, RSNA's metric, and clustering terminology, remove activation examples, and qualify the conclusion. A brief CUB subsection is added and references follow the acknowledgments without a separate page break. Most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is reduced and repositioned, while Table A.2 gains a row and explanatory footnote. Tables A.2–A.3 and Figure A.6 move from page 14 to page 13 through reflow. Existing figure content, including the remaining appendix visualizations, is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional ProtoPNet recipe makes the baseline comparison more informative, and CUB modestly broadens empirical support. Implementation disclosure and more cautious claims about human benefits improve transparency and interpretation. The gains are limited: CUB is documented briefly, and Figure 3 still displays only the original, lower-scoring ProtoPNet recipe.
